repository: XXRI OS Lite i686 Software Repository

source_priority_policy.principle: This repository is NOT a Tiny Core mirror. Tiny Core packages (tier 4) are a fallback used only when no modern official i686 AppImage, archive, or installer exists. The goal is the newest usable build of each app, not maximum package count. Every entry below carries a 'priority_tier' field so the store can see at a glance how modern/well-supported a given app's 32-bit build actually is.
source_priority_policy.hard_truth: Most major Linux software (Firefox, LibreOffice, Telegram, VLC's newest releases, etc.) has been actively dropping official 32-bit builds industry-wide over the last several years. For many apps the 'modern' answer is honestly 'the last official release that still shipped i686, frozen in time' rather than a current build. Entries reflect that honestly via 'last_official_i686_version' and 'upstream_32bit_status' rather than pretending a current 64-bit-only release has a 32-bit build it doesn't.

verification_methodology.summary: Two distinct kinds of 'verification' happen in this repository, and they must not be confused.
verification_methodology.research_verification: Performed by the AI assistant maintaining this file: confirming via live web search/fetch that a source page, release, or repository genuinely exists and states what it claims (e.g. 'this is the last official i686 build'). This is real, but it is NOT byte-level verification -- the assistant has no raw network access to download files, so it cannot independently confirm HTTP status codes, Content-Length, SHA256, or ELF architecture of any binary.
verification_methodology.byte_level_verification: Must be performed by running verify_sources.py (included alongside this file) in an environment with real network access. That script does actual HTTP HEAD/GET requests, hashes the downloaded bytes with SHA256, and for ELF binaries runs `file`/`readelf` to confirm the reported architecture (ELF32, EM_386/i686) rather than trusting the filename. Until that script has been run against a source, its live_check field is null and its status should be treated as 'unconfirmed bytes', regardless of how confident the research_verification note sounds.
verification_methodology.why_this_split_exists: An automated store that installs directly from this database must never be fed fabricated checksums or fabricated 'ELF verified' claims. The assistant will not write those fields as if they were checked when they were not -- doing so would be strictly worse than leaving them blank.
verification_methodology.checksum_policy: Where the upstream source publishes a live checksum file (e.g. Tiny Core's <pkg>.tcz.md5.txt), 'checksum.source_url' points at that official live file. Where no checksum has been independently computed, checksum.algorithm is null.
verification_methodology.icon_policy: Icons are never downloaded or re-hosted by this repository. icon_url points only at an official source (project website, project's own GitHub/GitLab repo, or official CDN/branding assets) in priority order. If no such official icon URL was confirmed, icon_url is null rather than pointing at a third-party mirror.

research_status_values.fully_verified: A currently-maintained official i686 build was found and confirmed live via search this session (byte-level verification still pending via verify_sources.py).
research_status_values.official_discontinued: The upstream project officially shipped i686 Linux builds in the past and has explicitly stated (in their own release notes/trackers/docs) that they stopped -- the last such version is recorded and used as the source.
research_status_values.verified_with_fallback: No qualifying official source exists (tiers 1-3 exhausted and rejected with cited reasons), so a tier-4/5 fallback (Tiny Core package or vetted community build) is selected and recorded instead.
research_status_values.research_in_progress: Sources exist and are recorded but the full priority-1-through-6 exhaustive search has not yet been completed to this session's standard.
research_status_values.not_found: Priorities 1 through 6 were all checked (official site, official archive/FTP, GitHub/GitLab Releases, distro repos including Tiny Core/Arch32/Debian/Ubuntu archives, trusted community AppImages, and Archive.org historical mirrors) and none yielded a usable i686 Linux build. Reasons and every checked source are recorded in rejection_reasons/checklist.

verification_methodology.test_status_fields: tested_install and tested_launch are always false in this repository -- they are placeholders for the XXRI Lite maintainer to flip to true only after physically testing the package on real i686 hardware or a VM. The assistant never sets these to true.
